title: Thinking Recursively (Part 1): Base Cases & Searching a List of Tuples
solutionExplanation: Demonstrates base-case handling on [] and recursive head/tail pattern matching for tuple search and member verification.

otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(N) time complexity with O(1) stack space under tail-call optimization.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does an Erlang recursive search function crash with {function_clause} if the base case find_product([], _) -> not_found is omitted?

options.label: When the list is exhausted, Erlang attempts to match the empty list [] against [Head | Tail], which fails
options.explanation: The cons pattern [Head | Tail] requires at least one element. An empty list cannot match it.

options.label: The BEAM scheduler halts because empty lists cannot exist in memory
options.explanation: Empty lists [] are the fundamental nil terminator in Erlang.

options.label: The garbage collector deletes the TargetId variable when a list reaches zero length
options.explanation: Variable bindings persist throughout the execution of the function clause.
